title: REPORT on human rights and democracy in the world and the European Union’s policy on the matter – annual report 2024
part_text: 15. Reiterates its concern regarding the increasing attacks on democratic principles, values and pluralism; stresses that the defence and support of democracy around the world is increasingly becoming of geopolitical and strategic interest; emphasises the importance of Parliament’s efforts in capacity-building for partner parliaments, promoting mediation and encouraging a culture of dialogue and compromise, especially among young political leaders, and empowering women parliamentarians, HRDs and representatives from civil society and independent media; reiterates its call on the Commission to continue its activities in these areas by allocating adequate funding and support to EU bodies, agencies and other grant-based organisations, ensuring that such support remains transparent, neutral and free from ideological bias or political interference; in this regard, expresses deep concern over instances of misuse of such funds, including through non-transparent lobbying, the promotion of specific ideologies and direct or indirect interference in the political processes of sovereign Member States; highlights recent cases where funds from international institutions, including the United States Agency for International Development and the EU, have reportedly been used to support groups engaging in political activism against democratically elected governments, including in Poland; calls for the EU to fully cooperate with the European Parliament, investigative journalists and public opinion in their efforts to clarify and address these unacceptable cases and urges the establishment of strict monitoring mechanisms to ensure that international aid and financial support, funded by taxpayers’ money, are used transparently, efficiently and in alignment with their intended objectives, in a manner consistent with democratic principles and respect for national sovereignty, free from interference in the political processes of the respective states; stresses the critical importance of directly supporting civil society and individuals expressing dissenting views, particularly in the current climate of growing global tensions and repression in increasing numbers of countries; reiterates the importance of EU election observation missions and Parliament’s contribution to developing and enhancing their methodology; calls for the development of an EU toolbox to be used in cases of disputed or non-transparent election results to prevent political and military crises in the post-election environment; calls for enhanced EU action to counter manipulative and false messages against the EU in election campaigns, in particular in countries that receive significant EU humanitarian and development assistance and in countries that are candidates for EU membership; calls for enhanced collaboration between Parliament’s Democracy Support and Election Coordination Group, the relevant Commission directorates-general and the EEAS;
